- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% for next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates downside; add 2–5% buffer to forecast lows for next 3–5 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75% of recent high), model frequently overcorrects downward; cap downward correction at 10% of spike magnitude.  
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish within 3 days, model often fails to adjust; apply mean reversion bias toward 30-day moving average for next 5 days.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overestimate early days (1–7) when sentiment is positive; reduce first 3 forecast points by 2–5% if sentiment >0.67.  
- If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is trending, model often misses mean reversion; add 1–3% downward bias for days 8–15 if sentiment remains flat.
